 JUDGMENT This judgment is emerged consequent upon the petition filed by the petitioners U/S 166 of M.V. Act,
claiming compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- on account of the death of Krishnappa, in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioners, in brief, is as follows:
On 14-11-2018 at about 1.30 p.m., the deceased was proceeding by riding his two-wheeler bearing No. KA-53-ET-2435 on NH-7, Bagepalli - Bengaluru road, near Harobade village gate, at that time the driver of Tata Ace Magic vehicle bearing No.KA-53-A-6268 driven the same at high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motorcycle of the deceased and caused the accident.
Due to the impact, the deceased fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
Immediately after the accident the deceased was shifted to Chikkaballapura Government Hospital, but deceased Krishnappa died on 15.11.2018 at 3.00 p.m.
Thereafter

postmortem was conducted and handed over the body to the petitioners and they have performed funeral and obsequies ceremonies and towards conveyance,
medicine, nourishment by spending an amount of Rs.50,000/- to Rs.75,000/-.

Prior to the accident, the deceased was hale and healthy aged about 55 years and was doing Building centering work and thereby earning Rs.1,000/- per day and contributing his entire earnings to the maintenance of the family.

Due to the untimely death of deceased the petitioners have suffered mentally and physically,
they have lost their bread earner.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending Tata Ace Magic vehicle bearing No.KA-53-A-6268
are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
Hence prays to award compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest.

3. In spite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 - owner has not appeared before the tribunal,
hence, he has been placed exparte.

sentences.text: After service of notice, the respondent No.2 insurance company appeared through its counsel, and filed its written statement by admitting issuance of policy to the Tata Ace Magic vehicle bearing No.KA-53-A-6268 and the liability of this respondent, if any, is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
Further contended that there is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
Further it has denied the cause and manner of accident and also involvement of the alleged offending vehicle in the alleged accident.
Further it has denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased.
The compensation as claimed by the petitioners is exorbitant and fanciful.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition against it.

met with an accident and succumbs to same due to negligence on the part of the driver of Tata Ace Magic bearing Reg. No.KA-53-A-6268 as alleged?
2.
Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount and from whom?
3 . What order or award?

Issue No.1: In the affirmative

The petitioners to prove their claim have produced true copies of FIR, spot mahazar, inquest report, PM report, IMV report, which are marked under Ex.P.1 to 5.
9.

As per the documents, Ex.P1 FIR is came to be registered on the basis of the first information given by one Sushilamma, who is the wife of deceased by alleging the rash and negligent driving by the driver of Tata Ace Magic vehicle bearing No.KA-53-A-6268.
The Ex.P1 is in consonance with the contents of petition wherein they have alleged about the negligence of driver of Tata Ace Magic vehicle bearing No.KA-53-A-6268.
In continuation of the investigation the IO has conducted spot mahazar as per Ex.P2.
On perusal of Ex.P2 the accident spot is in the left side edge of the road.
As per Ex.P.2 spot mahazar the IO has found the blood stains within 6 feet from the footpath.

It is alleged that the driver of Tata Ace bearing No.KA-53-A-6268 came from backside of vehicle of the deceased and by overtaking the vehicle of the deceased suddenly took left turn due to which the motorcycle of the deceased dashed against the backside of the offending Tata Ace vehicle.

Thus, the contents of Ex.P.2 discloses the actionable negligence of the driver of Tata Ace Magic vehicle bearing No.KA-53-A-6268.
10.
Further the Ex.P4 is the IMV report wherein the Tata Ace Magic vehicle bearing No.KA-53-A-6268 has got damages in its rear right side foot stepping channel.

On the other hand,
the two wheeler bearing No.KA-53-ET- 2435 has got damages in its front wheel, front mudguard,
front shock absorbing forks, head lamp assembly, front left indicator, both rear view mirrors,
steering handle bar, fuel tank was dented at right side.
The contents of Ex.P2 spot mahazar & Ex.P5 IMV report establishes that the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Tata Ace Magic vehicle bearing No.KA-53-A-6268.

This shows that the driver of Tata Ace Magic vehicle bearing No.KA-53-A- 6268 was negligent and caused the accident by suddenly taking his vehicle to the left side after overtaking the vehicle of the deceased.

The contents of spot mahazar and IMV report prima facie establishes the negligence of the driver of Tata Ace Magic vehicle bearing No.KA-53-A- 6268.
11.
In the accident cases, it is settled principle of law that "RES- IPSA LOQUITUR" which means the things speaks itself, is the standing principle to know the nature of the accident.
Under this principle how the negligence has to be infer is considered.

In tort law, "RES- IPSA LOQUITUR" principle that allows petitioners to meet their burden of proof with under which a court can infer negligence from the very nature of an accident or injury in the absence of direct evidence on how any defendant behaved in the context of tort litigation.

On perusal of Ex.P3- spot mahazar along with Ex.P4 IMV report wherein the damages of the vehicles involved in the accident is mentioned prima- facie shows the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending Tata Ace Magic vehicle bearing No.KA-53-A-6268.
Hence, by applying the said principle the negligence on the part of the driver of offending Tata Ace Magic vehicle bearing No.KA-53-A- 6268 is stands established.

12. It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the incident on basis of principle of preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered Sushelamma vs Manjamma on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154487892/
4 by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/
s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319

. Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 has observed that, it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.

Further the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Krishnappa and another reported in 2001 ACJ 1105,
where the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka considering the fact that the rider of the offending vehicle was not examined to prove any contributory negligence on the part of scooterist held that the accident had occurred due to rash or negligent driving by the rider of the offending van.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Krishnappa and another reported in 2001 ACJ 1105
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 13. Even here in this case the driver Tata Ace Magic vehicle bearing No.KA-53-A-6268 is not examined to show that there was no negligence on his part and even otherwise the IO, as already observed, has clearly opined that the accident occurred only due to the fault of the driver of the offending Tata Ace Magic vehicle bearing No.KA-53-A-6268 and he was charge sheeted.

14. In view of the ratio laid down in the authorities referred to above and applying the settled principle of law to the case at hand, which is further supported by the oral and documentary evidence adduced by PW-1, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the accident leading to this case indeed occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of offending Tata Ace Magic vehicle bearing No.KA-53-A-6268 resulting in the death of Sri Krishnappa.

15. The injuries sustained by the deceased is mentioned in Ex.P3 inquest and Ex.P4 postmortem,
which also evidentiates the nature of the accident and injuries sustained and caused of death of deceased due to shock and haemorrhage as a result of head injury sustained by him in the alleged accident.
16. The respondent No.2 has examined its official as RW.1 who has no personal knowledge about the accident.
Hence the evidence of RW1 does not helped the respondent No.2- insurance company in disproving the fact of the negligence as alleged by the petitioners.
17. As per well settled position of law the standard of proof in claim petition like present one, is only preponderance of probabilities.

Looking to the oral as well as documentary evidence of the petitioners there are sufficient materials to show that Sri Krishnappa died in the accident dated 14-11-2018 which is caused by the driver of the Tata Ace Magic vehicle bearing No.KA-53-A- 6268.
Accordingly issue No.1 answered in the affirmative.
ISSUE NO.2 18.
As held herein above, the petitioners have proved that Krishnappa died on 14-11-2018 due to the injuries sustained in RTA, which is caused by the driver of respondent No.1.

sentences.text: As contended in the petition the petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner No.2 to 4 are the children of the deceased Krishnappa.
The respondents do not specifically deny the relationship of petitioners with deceased.
The petitioners to prove their relationship with the deceased, have produced the notarized copies of Aadhar cards and voter ID card of petitioners which are marked under Ex.P7.
During the course of recording the evidence the notarized copies of Aadhar cards and voter ID car are compared with the original documents and found correct.

20. As per these documents the petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner No.2 to 4 are children of deceased Krishnappa but the respondents do not dispute the relationship of the petitioners with deceased.
The respondents do not dispute the Aadhar cards produced by the petitioners.
The respondents have not adduced any evidence to disprove the relationship of the petitioners with the deceased.

21. At the time of cross-examination and arguments the contention is raised by the respondent No.2 insurance company that the petitioner No.3 is the married daughter and the petitioner No.2 & 4 being the major sons are not entitled for compensation.

22. In this regard, in the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court reported in (2020) 11 SCC 356 between National Ins. Co. Ltd., V/s. Birender and others, wherein it is held as follows;
"A claim petition filed by major married and earning sons of the deceased mother,
the Honourable Supreme Court held as follows:
"12. The legal representatives of the deceased could move application for compensation by virtue of clause (c) of Section 166 (1).

entities.text: National Ins. Co. Ltd., V/s. Birender and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The major married son who is also earning and not fully dependent on the deceased would be still covered by the expression "legal representative" of the deceased.

This Court in Manjuri Bera (supra)
had expounded that liability to pay compensation under the Act does not cease because of absence of dependency of the concerned legal representative.
Notably, the expression "legal representative" has not been defined in the Act.
"It is thus settled by now that the legal representatives of the deceased have a right to apply for compensation.

Having said that, it must necessarily follow that even the major married and earning sons of the deceased being legal representatives have a right to apply for compensation and it would be the bounden duty of the Tribunal to consider the application irrespective of the fact whether the concerned legal representative was fully dependant on the deceased and not to limit the claim towards conventional heads only.

The evidence on record in the present case would suggest that the claimants were working as agricultural labourers on contract basis and were earning meagre income between Rs.1,00,000/ and Rs.1,50,000/ per annum.
In that sense, they were largely dependant on the earning of their mother and in fact, were staying with her, who met with an accident at the young age of 48 years".

sentences.text: The Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (in short, 'the Act') admittedly is a welfare statute for the betterment of the claimants.
No doubt, both the claimants are grown up and self-dependent but that does not mean or can be construed that they did not suffer any loss on account of sudden loss of both of their parents.

It has been rightly contended by learned counsel for the respondents/claimants that son and the daughter with the death of their parents have lost protection, physical as well as psychological, besides sense of fulfillment of having parents to look after and cater to their daily requirements of life and emotional support.

No doubt, the parents were senior citizens but one has to take a realistic approach that they would certainly be looking after their grand-children for their nurturing, psychological and physical well-being, and would be a source of joy and happiness for the entire family.
By this loss the family has lost companionship, and the pain and agony that has accompanied this sudden loss can never be compensated in terms of money.
One cannot ignore the fact that Surinder Kaur even in her advance age would be contributing her lot in the household chores, cooking food, cleaning and such like daily duties.

The family claims to be having agricultural land besides having milching cattle and therefore, in rural household it is a matter of common knowledge that women contribute towards looking after the cattle and agricultural produce and contribute their lot towards the source of earning from these fields.

The learned Tribunal has lost sight of the fact in not awarding compensation on account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses, which are handsomely part of calculations in such claim petitions.

Since there is no division of heads under which various amounts of compensation has been awarded, but having an overall look at the total compensation awarded in case of each of the deceased being ` 4.52 lacs and ` 3.50 lacs in lump sum and considering what has been left out as detailed in the Sushelamma vs Manjamma on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154487892/

7 foregoing lines, keeping in view the prevalent price index, there is no overwhelming occasion for this Court to show indulgence and thus this Court does not feel that the amount so awarded could be in any manner termed to be excessive necessitating intervention by this Court and rather appears to be just and appropriate in the prevalent scenario.
In the light of the same, the impugned award does not call for any interference and both the present appeals as such are disposed of as dismissed.
On the same point of law in the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Kerala reported in 2021 SCC Online Kerala 3209 (United India Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Shalumol and Others).

In this case also, as per the evidence available on record the deceased was doing Building centering work.
It shows that the income of the family of the deceased was meager as such even though the children are married and major they are certainly dependents on each other income.
Accordingly, in this case the petitioner No.2 to 4 being a major sons and daughter are entitled for the compensation in accordance with their dependency.

25. As held herein above, the petitioners have proved that Krishnappa died on 14-11-2018 due to the injuries sustained in RTA, which is caused by the driver of Tata Ace Magic vehicle bearing No.KA-53-A-6268.
26.
Now the quantum of compensation is to be decided.
As per Ex.P.7 - Aadhar card the date of birth of, deceased is 06-03-1950 and as per Voter ID card the deceased was aged about 41 years as on 01-01-1994.
In the postmortem and inquest the age of the deceased is shown as 55 years.
The age of the petitioner No.3 as per the cause title of the petition is 48 years.
Thereby if we rely on the date of birth mentioned in Ex.P.7 - Aadhar card as on the date of the accident the age of the deceased was 68 years.
27. As stated in the petition deceased was doing building centering work and earning Rs.1,000/- per day.
To prove the said fact, the petitioners have not produced any other evidence to establish the income of the deceased.
Such being the case, it is just and necessary to consider the notional income of the deceased at Rs.12,500/- p.m. as the accident is of the year 2018.

33. Liability:-
The respondent No.2 insurance company in its objection statement has admitted the issuance of policy to the offending vehicle.

Even though the respondent No.2 insurance company has taken contention that the driver of the offending vehicle was not having valid driving license at the time of accident, but no evidence is placed in this regard and the police has also not invoked any provisions or penal sections against the driver of offending vehicle in the charge sheet for driving the said vehicle without having license.
34. The respondent No.2 examined its official as RW.1 who produced Ex.R3 Form No.39 i.e., Permit extract.

By producing the said document the respondent No.2 insurance company contended that as on the date of accident i.e., on 14-11-2018 there was no valid permit for the offending vehicle bearing No. KA-53-A-6268 as such it cannot indemnify the liability of respondent No.1.
In this regard, the official i.e., RW.1 cross-examined by the learned counsel for the petitioner.

If we perused the Ex.R3 the permit for the offending vehicle was valid from 24.03.2013 to 23.03.2016, and the date of accident was 14-11-2018, thereby it is evident that as on the date of accident there was no valid permit for the offending vehicle.
35. The respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle remained exparte and has not made out any grounds to show that there was a valid permit at the time of accident.

The oral answers of RW.1 is not sufficient to consider that there was a valid permit for the offending vehicle at the time of accident because, the document produced at Ex.R3 being the public document clearly establishes that as on the date of accident, there was no valid permit for the offending vehicle bearing No. KA-53-A-6268.
36.

The respondent No.2 insurance company has taken specific defence of non existence of permit to the offending vehicle bearing No. KA-53-A-6268 and also taken steps to prove that, the offending vehicle has no permit at the time of accident.

Further in the copy of charge sheet which is available in the file shows that Sec. 192 of IMV Act is invoked by alleging the non-existing of the permit to the offending vehicle at the time of accident.

37. The charge sheet as well as the evidence of RW1 as per Ex.R3 clearly set out the aspect regarding non existence of the permit for the offending vehicle bearing No. KA-53-A-6268 at the time of accident.
The respondent No.1 -owner is placed exparte and has not adduced any evidence by showing the existence of permit to the offending vehicle.
Hence, the insurance company cannot be fastened with liability.

The learned counsel for the respondent relied on the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court reported in 2022 ACJ 2771 between Gohar Mohammed V/s U.P State Road Transportation Corporation & others wherein it is held as follows:
"8.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Having heard learned counsel for the parties and on perusal of the material available on record, it clearly reveals that on the date of accident, the appellant did not have a valid and effective permit to ply the offending vehicle on the route where Sushelamma vs Manjamma on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154487892/
10 accident took place.

Having extensively gone through the factfinding exercise, it is categorically recorded by MACT that the appellant was neither able to produce/prove the original permit nor was able to prove the information received under RTI Act.
Even if RTI information is considered by which it is not clear as to when the disputed permit was issued and by whom.

The alleged permit was issued on 28.07.2012, i.e.,
on Saturday and no explanation is on record as to why deposit of fee was asked on the next day i.e. Sunday.

Moreover, assuming that permit was valid as per letter of Transport Authority, but it does not of any help to the appellant since the vehicle was being plied on a route different than specified in permit.

The appellant has failed to give any explanation to refute the observations made by MACT to ply the vehicle on Roorkee bypass to Haridwar via Meerut which did not fall within the route of permit issued by Transport Authority.
The said findings of fact have been affirmed by the High Court by the impugned order.

9. After going through the record, the concurrent findings of fact do not warrant any interference since they do not outrageously defy the logic as to suffer from the vice of irrationality and neither incur the blame of being perverse.
In view of foregoing discussion, we are of the considered opinion that the arguments raised by appellant are bereft of any merit, hence this appeal is hereby dismissed".
38. By keeping the arguments canvassed by both the parties in background, there is no dispute that at the time of accident the offending vehicle bearing No. KA-53- A-6268 was covered with insurance.
But the violation of the condition of insurance policy is stands established as there was no permit for the offending vehicle at the time of accident.

39. In this case, the respondent No.1 owner of the offending vehicle bearing No. KA-53-A-6268 even after the service of summons has not lead any evidence to show that he has not violated the policy condition willfully.

Thereby the conduct of respondent No.1 -owner allowing the offending vehicle bearing No. KA-53-A-6268 to ply on the road without permit is a breach of policy condition and thereby the insurance company cannot be fastened with liability.
The respondent No.1 being the owner cannot take the benefit of his own wrong.

Under such circumstances, the insurance company cannot be fastened with liability of pay and recover when there is clear breach of rules of IMV Act and liability to pay compensation is on the respondent No.1 owner.
Hence, the respondent No.1 owner is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
The petitioner is entitle for compensation with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
Accordingly, this issue answered in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.4:-
40.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
In the accident cases, it is settled principle of law that "RES- IPSA LOQUITUR" which means the things speaks itself, is the standing principle to know the nature of the accident.
In tort law, "RES- IPSA LOQUITUR" principle that allows petitioners to meet their burden of proof with under which a court can infer negligence from the very nature of an accident or injury in the absence of direct evidence on how any defendant behaved in the context of tort litigation.
On perusal of Ex.P3- spot mahazar along with Ex.P4 IMV report wherein the damages of the vehicles involved in the accident is mentioned prima- facie shows the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending Tata Ace Magic vehicle bearing No.KA-53-A-6268.
Hence, by applying the said principle the negligence on the part of the driver of offending Tata Ace Magic vehicle bearing No.KA-53-A- 6268 is stands established.
. Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 has observed that, it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
Hence the evidence of RW1 does not helped the respondent No.2- insurance company in disproving the fact of the negligence as alleged by the petitioners.
17. As per well settled position of law the standard of proof in claim petition like present one, is only preponderance of probabilities.
The Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (in short, 'the Act') admittedly is a welfare statute for the betterment of the claimants.
No doubt, both the claimants are grown up and self-dependent but that does not mean or can be construed that they did not suffer any loss on account of sudden loss of both of their parents.
No doubt, the parents were senior citizens but one has to take a realistic approach that they would certainly be looking after their grand-children for their nurturing, psychological and physical well-being, and would be a source of joy and happiness for the entire family.
By this loss the family has lost companionship, and the pain and agony that has accompanied this sudden loss can never be compensated in terms of money.
One cannot ignore the fact that Surinder Kaur even in her advance age would be contributing her lot in the household chores, cooking food, cleaning and such like daily duties.
The family claims to be having agricultural land besides having milching cattle and therefore, in rural household it is a matter of common knowledge that women contribute towards looking after the cattle and agricultural produce and contribute their lot towards the source of earning from these fields.
On the same point of law in the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Kerala reported in 2021 SCC Online Kerala 3209 (United India Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Shalumol and Others).
23. Further with regard to the married daughters right of claiming compensation in the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court reported in AIR 2007 SC 1474 in the case of Manjura Beri V. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. Wherein it was held that even a married daughter can seek compensation.
24.

Accordingly, in this case the petitioner No.2 to 4 being a major sons and daughter are entitled for the compensation in accordance with their dependency.
